title: Practical Skill-Proof: Multi-Table Revenue by Customer Tier
prompt: The business executive team wants to understand how spending is distributed across customer tiers. Write a SQL query to calculate the total sales revenue (quantity * unit_price) grouped by customer tier ('Gold', 'Silver', 'Bronze'). Your result must return columns `tier` and `total_revenue`, sorted by `total_revenue` descending.
starter_code:
-- Write your query joining customers, orders, and order_items
SELECT 
    c.tier,
    SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue
FROM customers c
-- Complete the JOIN and GROUP BY logic below
canonical_buggy_query:
SELECT 
    c.tier, 
    SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue
FROM customers c, orders o, order_items oi
GROUP BY c.tier
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;
canonical_correct_query:
SELECT 
    c.tier, 
    SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue
FROM customers c
INNER JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
INNER JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
GROUP BY c.tier
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

sql_aggregations.name: Aggregations & Grouping
sql_aggregations.criteria: Proper calculation using SUM(quantity * unit_price) and grouping by c.tier with ORDER BY total_revenue DESC.

sql_joins.name: Relational Multi-Table JOIN Logic
sql_joins.criteria: Explicit relational joins between customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id AND orders.order_id = order_items.order_id without Cartesian product.
